description: Simulated semiconductor trade flow and dependency data for Taiwan Strait demo

commodities.name: advanced logic chips (<7nm)
commodities.notes: EU and US auto, AI, and defense electronics rely on Taiwan fabs for leading-edge nodes.

commodities.name: wafer fabrication equipment (EUV lithography)
commodities.notes: ASML shipments to Taiwan fabs are a critical bottleneck for advanced capacity expansion.

commodities.name: mature-node PMIC / MCU
commodities.notes: Secondary chokepoint if strait logistics degrade even without fab damage.

chokepoints.name: TSMC Hsinchu advanced fabs
chokepoints.impact_if_disrupted: Global AI accelerator and smartphone SoC production severely constrained within weeks.

chokepoints.name: Taiwan Strait shipping lanes
chokepoints.impact_if_disrupted: Delayed equipment imports, outbound finished wafer shipments, and packaging material flows.

chokepoints.name: Kaohsiung export terminals
chokepoints.impact_if_disrupted: Inventory accumulation at fabs, customer allocation disputes, spot price spikes.

dependency_summary: EU and US supply chains show HIGH structural dependency on Taiwan for advanced semiconductors. TSMC Hsinchu fabs produce approximately 90% of the world's sub-7nm chips. Cross-strait tension elevates substitution risk because alternative capacity (US, Japan, Korea) lacks equivalent leading-edge volume before 2028–2030 in most planning scenarios.
